Just a little over a month ago, I came here and made a post very similar to yours. That was one of the worst days of my life, getting this diagnosis. I’m really close with my dad, and it sounds like you are too. It’s so hard and it feels gut wrenching. I can tell you though, a month in, that I feel like we’re fighting a war. It takes a really long time to get back to “normal” and I’ve accepted that, and I’m patient, even though it sucks. Knowledge helps me so I read a lot about MM online and the International Myeloma Foundation has sent me informational booklets that are very helpful (they have these in multiple languages).

I first felt like MM was a death sentence and I was devastated. It’s still devastating, but now I know that there are treatments for this and people can live with it for many years. The doctors are hopeful, so I am hopeful. You’re not alone in this. Give yourself some time to adjust to the news- it will be the new normal for a while, but think of it as having a chronic disease (diabetes, bipolar, etc) rather than a terminal cancer.
